candidate.explanation: v13 launch-hardening candidate, cut 2026-08-03 on branch v13 after SC-P0-01..06 and SC-P1-07,08,10,11,12 landed. It contains everything in the prior candidate a11afda PLUS: fail-closed entitlement so a transient Supabase failure can never read as 'Free' or create a duplicate checkout (271e31c), highest-valid-entitlement resolution across overlapping subscriptions (ebcfe5c), one server catalog deciding displayed AND charged currency with no silent cross-currency retry (6380016), production launch config that fails closed WITHOUT relying on a flag (6debd63), removal of the legacy client-email customer route and arbitrary portal returnUrl (77cee5b), react-router-dom 6.30.4 -> 7.18.2 with centralized internal-path validation (ca3eaa8), a zero-warning React correctness pass with a stale-response guard on every id-keyed studio loader (de9c779), typed error-to-copy states across billing/generation/export (f4394a9), sharper honest landing copy (45ec316), the billing state-contract matrix + trial-eligibility coverage (709015a), and the capped-beta value scorecard (879e1bb). Every automated check that can run without production secrets was re-run at this exact commit 879e1bb on 2026-08-03. IMPORTANT: unlike the a11afda cut, the production configuration gate CANNOT be carried forward this time — SC-P0-04 changed backend/lib/launch-config.js by ~200 lines and backend/scripts/release-check.js, so the 2026-07-28 production /api/admin/readiness result no longer describes this candidate's config-gate code and must be re-observed against the deployed candidate. Documentation-only commits after this SHA (including this launch-state record) do not invalidate the candidate; anything under backend/, app-src/, app/, e2e/, api/ or config does.

checks.name: Authenticated seeded browser matrix
checks.scope_rationale: Scoped to public launch on 2026-07-28. The owner has walked the signed-in product in production — signup, login, Stripe trial, access, cancel, AI generation and lifecycle email — and it works (docs/evidence/2026-07-28-owner-production-walkthrough.md). What the matrix adds over one person clicking the happy path is phone and keyboard operation, cross-account isolation driven in a real browser, and the failure paths (session expiry, provider timeout mid-generation, reload during export). A supervised cohort of invited accounts with the owner watching can absorb those; strangers arriving unannounced cannot. So it stays required for public_paid.

checks.name: Production configuration gate
checks.note: OBSERVED IN PRODUCTION AND FAILING. SC-P0-04 (6debd63) rewrote backend/lib/launch-config.js (~200 lines) so production config fails closed automatically, and SC-P0-03 (6380016) added the currency-catalog completeness rule, so the 2026-07-28 readiness observation could not be carried forward. GET /api/admin/readiness was re-run in production against the deployed v13 config-gate code (2026-08-03): mode=production, ready=FALSE, blockers=1. Thirteen of fourteen checks pass (migrations present, stripe:price_allowlist all live prices set, cron:secret set, email:delivery configured, ai:spend_ceiling $15, launch:unsafe_bypass not set; live signals all ok — outbox_backlog 0, webhook_failures_24h 0, reservation_leakage 0). The single failing check is launch:config: 'currency: EUR_PRICING_ENABLED set without EUR_PRICES_VERIFIED (run npm run verify-prices)'. This is the new SC-P0-03 guardrail working exactly as intended: EUR pricing is live in production (the v12 rehearsal charged EUR), but the one-time EUR price verification flag was never set, so the gate fails closed rather than risk showing EUR and charging USD. OWNER ACTION to clear (single, concrete): run `npm run verify-prices` with the LIVE Stripe key (read-only — proves every plan/currency pair's amount, product, interval, active status) and, when it passes, set EUR_PRICES_VERIFIED=1 in the production environment, then re-run GET /api/admin/readiness (expect ready=true, 0 blockers). Alternatively, if EUR is not intended live, unset EUR_PRICING_ENABLED. Until readiness reports ready=true this check is honestly failed and the machine gate is NO-GO — the gate caught a real production config gap.

blockers.title: react-router / react-router-dom 7.18.2 carry an open high advisory GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 (RSC-mode CSRF bypass)
blockers.closure: GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 is fixed only in react-router 8.3.0, which removes the react-router-dom package and requires React 19 / Vite 7 / Node >=22.22 — a stack upgrade beyond v13's scope. `npm audit --omit=dev` reports 2 high at 879e1bb. NOT reachable in practice: the advisory states it only affects applications using the unstable RSC APIs, and this app ships no RSC or SSR entry point (declarative BrowserRouter only). Close by either (a) owner accepting the risk with a named rationale and revisit date, or (b) upgrading to react-router 8 on a React 19 / Vite 7 migration. Until then it is an open, named, unreachable risk — it must not be reported as closed. Introduced alongside SC-P0-06 (ca3eaa8), which closed the three previously-open 6.30.4 advisories.

public_paid.note: NO-GO computed by `npm run launch:gate`. Beyond the capped-beta blocker (release_config failed — production readiness re-observed 2026-08-03 returned ready=false because EUR_PRICING_ENABLED is set without EUR_PRICES_VERIFIED), public paid also carries: the open high router advisory GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 (blocker P1-router-rsc-csrf-advisory, not reachable — no RSC — but not accepted and not closed), plus the two long-standing accepted risks that a full GO can never absorb (authenticated browser matrix skipped, nine-transition live-money rehearsal not_run). how_to_create_a_new_candidate: 1. Land all intended work on the release branch. No feature work after this point.
2. Set candidate.sha to the exact frozen commit and candidate.state to "frozen".

3. Re-run every required check at that SHA and record status, observed_at_sha and an evidence reference for each. A check whose underlying code changed since the last candidate may NOT be carried forward — re-run it or mark it not_run.
4. Attach owner evidence references for the live items.
5. Run `npm run launch:gate`. It recomputes both verdicts; it cannot be argued with.
6. Run `npm run launch:render` to regenerate docs/LAUNCH_STATE.md.

Any commit after step 2 that changes code creates a NEW candidate: the SHA no longer matches HEAD, every check pinned to the old SHA stops counting, and the verdict returns to NO-GO. Documentation-only commits (docs/ and the prompt packs) do not.
